10.1c — 2-Button Jam: Build Day 2

Yesterday's loop exists (10.1b); today either becomes a GAME: the sticky-note task first (the one that could kill you), one more system, and the first difficulty ramp. By close of class the jam is shippable — everything tomorrow adds is bonus.

Build Day ~50 min

Order of the day:

  1. Sticky note first (15 min, hard cap). The riskiest thing from yesterday — the wall of text? The moving obstacle? The enemy that respects your verbs? BUILD IT NOW. If the cap expires and it still does not work: cut the feature, not the cap. That decision is the whole skill of jamming.
  2. One more system (15 min). Score, health, or a second obstacle TYPE — exactly one. Systems are verbs' consequences; two verbs × three contexts is a whole game if each context teaches something new.
  3. Ramp the difficulty (10 min). Your 7.5a beat chart, compressed: the game should be trivial at second 5 and demanding at second 45. Same shapes, tighter timing, one new thing at a time.
  4. Playtest cross-team (10 min). Two minutes with a NON-team member — silent watching, 2.4a rules. Fix nothing; write it down. Tomorrow (10.1d) is the playtest day, so today's two minutes are just a smoke test of the ramp.

Bug Hunt: Day-2 traps

  1. The game "needs" a menu. Does it? What does a jam game ACTUALLY need at second zero — and what does a title screen give you that a distinctive first screen does not?
  2. Your second system interacts with the loop in a way nobody predicted (score on death? health on dash?). When do you decide: feature, bug, or delight? (Answer rule: if a tester laughs, it is a delight; if a tester asks WHY, it is a bug.)
  3. The ramp made second 5 too hard (you only play your own game — 9.6a observer effect, again). Who must be able to play second 5 blind?
Close of Day ~5 min

Tinker: Shippable check

  1. Define shippable out loud: both verbs + 3 contexts + a ramp + a lose state + a RESTART. Do you have it? Commit + push: "10.1c: game (shippable)".
  2. Write the polish wishlist for 10.1e — ranked, and each item tagged 1-hour or 10-minute. Ten-minute items ship; one-hour items are lies.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain what your sticky-note risk was and how it resolved
  • Ship the second system inside the day's cap
  • Show a difficulty ramp a stranger can feel
  • Declare shippable honestly, with a ranked wishlist
